title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
layout_note: Left part: an input-layer card stack (C channels) holding a 4-node graph X1-X4, coloured lines bundling into a dashed 'hidden layers' gap, and an output-layer card stack (F maps) holding the same graph as Z1-Z4, with labels Y1 and Y4 to its right. Right part: a separate t-SNE scatter of learned node embeddings, coloured by class.
grouping: Each layer is a stack of white rounded rectangles offset like a deck of cards, corner-labelled C or F; the same graph is drawn inside both stacks, and each node keeps its own colour (blue, orange, green, purple) in both layers and in its curved connection lines.
shapes_depth: Flat vector: nodes are circles with a pale tint and a darker outline of the same hue, edges thin black lines; layers are layered card outlines that suggest channel depth; curved coloured lines converge to a single dashed line and fan out again.
proposed_highlight: No separate highlight; the method is shown by drawing the graph structure identically in the input and output layers (shared over layers) and attaching labels Y only to two output nodes with dashed double arrows, showing semi-supervision.
lesson: To show a graph network, draw the same small graph inside each layer, keep one colour per node across layers, and attach supervision only to the few labelled nodes with dashed double arrows.
notes: Venue from the first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2017'). The right third of the figure is a results-style t-SNE plot, not part of the schematic.

arrangement.units: a schematic panel (two card stacks for input and output layers joined across a whitespace gap labelled 'hidden layers') and an unframed scatter-plot panel on the right, separated only by whitespace
arrangement.inputs_as: a small 4-node graph with node features X1-X4 inside the input-layer card stack
arrangement.losses_at: right of the output layer: dashed double-headed arrows from Z1 and Z4 to label nodes Y1 and Y4, coloured like their nodes
arrangement.shared: the graph structure (black edges) is redrawn identically inside the input and output layer stacks

insights.structure: Two card-stack layers (input C, output F) hold the same 4-node graph and face each other across a narrow gap marked 'hidden layers', with label nodes Y outside the output stack and a scatter plot filling the right third.
insights.data: Node features and outputs are tinted circles with math labels (X_i, Z_i), channel depth is the offset stack of card outlines, and the result is a dense t-SNE scatter of coloured dots.
insights.emphasis: Per-node colours carried through the connecting lines and dashed label arrows make the propagation and the partial labelling the visible point; there is no highlight box.
insights.flow: Left-to-right: each input node sends a curved line in its colour that converges into one dashed line through the hidden-layer gap, then fans out to its matching output node.
insights.avoid: The t-SNE panel sits in the same figure without a divider or label, and its class colours (red, yellow, grey, etc.) are unrelated to the node colours of the schematic, inviting a false match.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
